text.p: PRAVDA - Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said government spending within last year's state budget did not create inflationary pressures.
- He said the government was not responsible for the recent jump in interbank interest rates.

- Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar said he had no information about the new owners of oil and gas storage company Nafta. The privatisation of Nafta raised eyebrows last August when the state National Property Fund sold its entire stake of 45.9 percent to an unknown company, Druha Obchodna.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The association of Slovak health insurance companies said most domestic insurers had large deficits.
- Slovakia's production of corn is expected to total 784,100 tonnes in 1997, up from 596,600 tonnes last year.

SME - The opposition Democratic Union (DU) welcomed postponement of banking privatisation, saying the ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS) had planned to use the banks to strengthen in power.

NARODNA OBRODA - More than two-thirds of Slovaks support direct presidential elections, according an opinion poll. About 20 percent of those polled said they would support parliamentary elections of the president.
- The Association of Securities Traders said it would initiate the creation of a law on protecting minority shareholder rights this year.
- DU deputy Viliam Vaskovic criticised the creation of an export-import bank outside the scrutiny of the supervision of the National Bank of Slovakia.
